metadata.title: Replication package for "Synthetic Corruptions Underestimate Real Forgetting in Object Detection: Measuring the Offset and the Limits of Feature Distance"
metadata.description:
Replication package for the paper "Synthetic Corruptions Underestimate Real Forgetting in Object Detection: Measuring the Offset, and Why Feature Distance Alone Cannot Predict It".

 The archive contains everything needed to re-derive every number in every table and figure of the paper without a GPU and without re-training: all experiment and analysis scripts, the corruption recipes, the split listings for every arm, every result CSV behind every table and figure, and the cached feature matrices for the base, real and synthetic sets of all five deployments together with all 25 corrupted severity sets.


Two verification scripts re-derive every numerical claim in the paper directly from those CSVs and print a per-claim pass or fail. They run straight out of the archive with no configuration and report "48 checks, 0 failed" and "63 checks, 0 failed" on the archived data. Because the features are cached, the direction scoring, the six-metric comparison, both space ablations, the calibration fits and all three figures reproduce on a CPU in minutes without access to the original images.


The real-world shift datasets (ExDark, DAWN, EXWOD, FLIR ADAS) are third-party public resources used under their own licences and are NOT redistributed here. Only derived feature matrices and the file-name listings of each split are included, so a reader can reconstruct the exact splits after obtaining the datasets from their original sources.
See README.md inside the archive for the directory map and run instructions.

hits.title: Replication package for "Synthetic Corruptions Underestimate Real Forgetting in Object Detection: Measuring the Offset and the Limits of Feature Distance"

metadata.title: Replication package for "Who absorbs a crisis in the profession? Gender versus task exposure among Korean teachers"
metadata.description:
This archive is the replication package for the article "Who absorbs a crisis in the profession? Gender versus task exposure among Korean teachers" (Junhee Lee). It contains the full estimation chain, the saved estimation results, every derived output reported in the article, and the manuscript itself.

WHAT IS HERE

The chain runs from a single entry point, code/00_run_all.do. The archive holds the analysis code, the saved Stata estimation results, the LaTeX table fragments and figure files that the manuscript inputs, the estimate macros the manuscript prints, and the per-script logs the chain leaves behind on normal termination. hashes.json records a SHA-256 digest for each file so that any copy can be checked against the deposited state. manuscript/main.pdf is the article the archive belongs to.

Start with README.md for the layout and the entry point, REPLICATION.md for the artifact-to-script crosswalk and the documented boundaries, and CODEBOOK.md for variable construction and data notes.

WHAT IS NOT HERE

The underlying microdata are not included. The Korean Teacher Longitudinal Study-Elementary School Teacher (KTLS-E) is licensed research data held by the Korean Educational Development Institute and cannot be redistributed by the author; researchers may apply for access through the institute's data service. The archive therefore permits inspection and value-by-value verification of every reported number against the saved estimates, but not re-estimation without an independent licence.

A small number of logs are withheld where they would disclose frequency cells below the disclosure threshold, or where they are not chain output; REPLICATION.md names each exclusion and its reason.

LICENCE

code/ is released under the MIT Licence. output/, manuscript/, data/ and the three Markdown documents are released under CC BY 4.0. The KTLS-E microdata are covered by neither and are not distributed. See LICENSE in the archive; the record-level licence field records CC BY 4.0 for the archive as a whole.

RELATION TO THE PREVIOUS VERSION

The analysis chain is unchanged from the previous version: code/ and output/ are identical, and the estimate macros the manuscript prints are byte-for-byte the same. What changed is the manuscript and the accompanying documentation — the article's title, its length, and its reference list, together with the corresponding updates to README.md, REPLICATION.md and CODEBOOK.md. No estimate in the article has changed.
keywords: teacher labor markets gender difference-in-differences identity equivalence testing replication package Stata Korea

hits.title: Replication package for "Who absorbs a crisis in the profession? Gender versus task exposure among Korean teachers"

metadata.title: Replication Code for "Social Media Investor Sentiment and the Hang Seng Tech Index: Asymmetric Bidirectional Predictability and Regime Dependence"
metadata.description:
This package reproduces every table and figure in the paper "Social Media Investor Sentiment and the Hang Seng Tech Index: Asymmetric Bidirectional Predictability and Regime Dependence".

The study builds a daily attention-weighted Sentiment Tone Index (STI) from Eastmoney Guba posts on the top-10 HSTECH constituents (January 2022 to December 2024), estimates a VAR(3) with Granger tests, impulse responses and variance decompositions, and estimates regime dependence with state-dependent local projections carrying a bull/bear interaction.

Contents:

hstech_sentiment_analysis.ipynb: a Colab notebook running the full analysis in five sections (baseline VAR, robustness, bootstrap, overnight and out-of-sample checks, local projections).

var_panel_daily.csv: the 726-trading-day panel (sentiment index, index returns, macro controls, attention volume, overnight sentiment). In the file the first-differenced exchange rate and SHIBOR are named RRMB and RSHIBOR.

analysis_scripts.zip: the same analysis as five standalone Python scripts, with a README, requirements.txt, and data_prep.py documenting how the panel was built from the raw post file.

Requirements: Python 3 with numpy, pandas, statsmodels, scipy and matplotlib (see requirements.txt). To run the notebook in Colab, upload var_panel_daily.csv to Google Drive (My Drive root). To run the scripts locally, keep the csv in a data subfolder next to the scripts. A full run takes about ten minutes.

hits.title: Replication Code for "Social Media Investor Sentiment and the Hang Seng Tech Index: Asymmetric Bidirectional Predictability and Regime Dependence"

metadata.title: Replication package for "The Window, Not the Tail: Measurement Bias in Rolling Quantile Connectedness and the Limits of State-Conditioned Spillover Indices"
metadata.description:
Complete replication code for the paper "The Window, Not the Tail: Measurement Bias in Rolling Quantile Connectedness and the Limits of State-Conditioned Spillover Indices".

The package reproduces every table and figure end to end in approximately four minutes on four cores. It implements:

- Generalised forecast error variance decompositions and Diebold-Yilmaz connectedness measures
- A time-varying parameter VAR estimated by Kalman filtering with forgetting factors
- Quantile VAR connectedness, including a warm-started rolling estimator
- The regime-quantile concordance index and its linear Gaussian null benchmark
- Identification controls: a common-estimator specification and a random-subsample null
- Lead-lag AUROC profiles and a full expanding-window out-of-sample protocol
- Statistical tests: DeLong, Clark-West, Giacomini-White, Kupiec, Christoffersen, Engle-Manganelli DQ, Romano-Wolf
- Economic value and value-at-risk backtesting
- All figures

Data are from public sources (Yahoo Finance, FRED, iShares, Investing.com) and are not redistributed here; see README.md for the series identifiers and construction steps.

Runs on Python 3.10+ with numpy, pandas, scipy, matplotlib and openpyxl.

hits.title: Replication package for "The Window, Not the Tail: Measurement Bias in Rolling Quantile Connectedness and the Limits of State-Conditioned Spillover Indices"

metadata.title: Replication Package - What Aggregate Mutation Scores Hide: A Mutant-Level Analysis of LLM-Generated Unit Tests Across Prompt Engineering Strategies
metadata.description:
This repository contains the complete replication package for an empirical study investigating the impact of prompt engineering strategies on the quality of unit test suites generated by Large Language Models (LLMs).

The study evaluates five prompt engineering strategies (Zero-Shot, One-Shot, Few-Shot, Program of Thoughts, and Chain of Code) applied to three LLMs (Llama 4 Maverick, Qwen3 Coder 480B A35B, and Grok Code Fast 1, accessed via OpenRouter API) across 16 Java classes drawn from Defects4J and TestBench. Test suite quality is assessed through mutation testing using PIT, following the experimentation framework proposed by Wohlin et al.

The package includes: the Dockerfile and environment configuration used to run the experiments; all scripts for experiment creation, mutation testing execution, and test suite analysis; the complete set of prompts (in Portuguese, as executed, and translated into English) and generated artifacts for each of the 16 experimental subjects; and the raw cost data for LLM API usage.

This artifact supports a paper submitted to the Journal of Systems and Software (JSS), titled "What Aggregate Mutation Scores Hide: A Mutant-Level Analysis of LLM-Generated Unit Tests Across Prompt Engineering Strategies."

See the README file for detailed instructions on environment setup, execution, and expected outputs.

hits.title: Replication Package - What Aggregate Mutation Scores Hide: A Mutant-Level Analysis of LLM-Generated Unit Tests Across Prompt Engineering Strategies

metadata.title: Calibrating Selective LLM Escalation Claims in C/C++ Vulnerability Triage: A Cost-Tuned-Comparator Empirical Study - Replication Package (v1.0.23)
metadata.description: Replication package for the empirical study of selective local-LLM escalation for software vulnerability triage. Contains the screening and selective-escalation pipeline, gate/merge recomputation scripts, statistical-analysis code, table- and figure-generation scripts, cached per-sample reports, figure sources, and environment notes. Manuscript tables and figures rebuild offline from the cached per-sample reports without rerunning LLM inference or external-corpus preprocessing, subject to three exceptions the package documents: the validation-locked 200-sample rows are released as aggregates only, the cross-dataset deduplication-match ledger is withheld with the raw corpora it embeds, and the simultaneous bootstrap bands ship as precomputed band tables rather than replicate arrays. Source code is released under the MIT License; cached data-derived outputs are released under CC-BY-4.0. Third-party model weights and external datasets (PrimeVul, BigVul, DiverseVul, ReVeal) are not redistributed; the package identifies their sources and provides the preprocessing and loading scripts used in the study.

metadata.title: Replication package: what if acquisitions do not raise systematic risk?
metadata.description:
Scripts, pre-registrations, run logs and deal-level estimates for a study of acquirer systematic risk covering 38,991 completed acquisitions by listed acquirers across 37 countries, 2007-2025.

The package includes every script that produces a number in the manuscript or its supplement, under its working filename, together with the pre-registration written before each analysis was executed and the log of the run as it happened. NUMBERS.md maps each reported figure to the script that produces it, and states whether that script runs on the data included here.

Return series licensed from LSEG Datastream, and firm and deal characteristics licensed from Bureau van Dijk Orbis, are not redistributable: they are documented rather than included. LICENCE_AND_DATA.md classifies every column by source and explains how to rebuild what is excluded. Five scripts, including the one that produces the headline estimate, run on the derived data provided.

Author identification is withheld during double-blind peer review and will be added on acceptance.

hits.title: Replication package: what if acquisitions do not raise systematic risk?
